A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MapReduce LoRA and RaTE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F support reliable comparison; the appendices are unchanged apart from pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video generation experiments, language-task evaluations, merge-frequency ablations, and RaTE experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a one-merge condition to the fixed-budget ablation in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The iterative training and merging procedure, RaTE distillation objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–3. Testing one merge adds an experimental condition rather than revising the method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same image-generation datasets and evaluations, video-generation tasks, and Reddit Summary and Helpful Assistant language tasks. The added merge-count condition introduces no new dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds the k=1 one-shot-merging comparator to the existing k=4 versus k=10 fixed-budget comparison. Comparator membership in the broader image, video, and language benchmarks remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The merge-frequency evaluation expands from k={4,10} to k={1,4,10}. It retains the fixed training budgets and mixed-precision evaluation; no changes to the existing benchmark protocols are reported.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Figure 6 extend the merge-frequency ablation to test one-shot merging against repeated merging under equal total training steps. The RaTE token-count ablation and appendix analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the video evaluation's four samples per prompt with shared fixed seeds and mean-score reporting. The added ablation condition introduces no new repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Figure 6 newly reports k=1 post-merge scores of 0.79 GenEval, 22.324 PickScore, and 0.8274 OCR. Section 4.4 adds the corresponding comparisons with k=10; the existing k=4 and k=10 curves and Tables 1–6 retain their results.

T1.justification: The proximal-averaging formulation, Polyak–Łojasiewicz assumption, convergence reasoning in Equations 3–8, and RaTE loss in Equation 9 are unchanged. No definitions, assumptions, or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about advancing Pareto fronts, composable preference control, cross-modal performance, and untargeted-reward generalization. The added ablation supports existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 changes from describing k=4 and k=10 as similar to interpreting the expanded comparison as showing consistently better final performance and reduced merging degradation with more iterations. The other interpretations and Appendix F limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project repository link on the title page, providing code-access information absent from v1. Appendix C's implementation settings, hardware information, and model-access links are unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to prior RLHF, multi-objective optimization, LoRA, and model-merging research remain unchanged. Reference-list differences concern pagination rather than added or removed works.

P1.justification: The merge-frequency paragraph in Section 4.4 receives a localized rewrite and the title page gains a repository address. The section organization and nearly all remaining prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 6 expands from six to nine panels by adding the k=1 row and updating its caption. The resulting layout reflow includes moving Table 4 to the following page; other figures and appendix displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: Adding the one-shot condition under the same training budget strengthens the empirical case for repeated merging beyond v1's four-versus-ten comparison. The repository pointer also improves access information. These are useful, limited gains; the method, principal benchmark results, theory, and appendix evidence remain unchanged.
